subject: Dedicated sizing impact on reserved term and GPU-cost sensitivity — Teladyne pilot
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: ops@teladyne.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing impact on reserved term and GPU-cost sensitivity — Teladyne pilot

Hi Rebecca / Teladyne ops team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. As requested, attached is a concise reserved capacity proposal that ties the dedicated sizing recommendation to a set of pricing sensitivity guardrails. High-level summary:

- Recommended starting pool: 16x H100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (single region, us-west).
- Typical QPS range: 12–28 concurrent inference streams depending on peak windows; forecasted average utilization 58% over first 3 months (see attached forecast).
- Term options we modeled: 12 / 24 / 36 months. Our economics show the 24-month term hits the best tradeoff between unit price and risk exposure for both sides.

Key pricing sensitivity questions for you:
1) Do you have a hard ceiling for discounts (e.g., procurement approval threshold >20%)?
2) Are you comfortable with an indexation clause that adjusts per-unit pricing if a public GPU market index moves +/- X%?

Attachments: Redwood_Reserved_Capacity_Proposal_v2.pdf (detailed sizing + scenario math). Please review the scenario sheet and send over the procurement thresholds your team requires (approval levels, preferred index, any escrow/hedge preferences).

Next steps: can we lock a 30-minute sync early next week to align on the preferred term and approval path so we can prepare final commercial language?

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0187

From: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@teladyne.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@teladyne.ai, ops@teladyne.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing impact on reserved term and GPU-cost sensitivity — Teladyne pilot

Sofia,

Thanks for the proposal — useful level of detail. A few notes from procurement/ops after an initial review:

- Procurement approval thresholds: discounts up to 15% can be signed by our procurement lead. Anything >15% requires VP Procurement sign-off; anything >25% requires CFO approval.
- We need a clearer protection for upward GPU cost shocks. If public GPU spot prices rise >20% within the first 12 months, we need an option to either reduce committed capacity or trigger a bilateral re-price conversation.
- Conversely, if GPU market prices fall materially (>=15%), we prefer a rebate/true-up or a mid-term reset option rather than clawbacks.

I've attached a rough internal forecast (teladyne_usage_forecast.xlsx) that shows a steeper ramp in months 3–6 if the pilot KPIs are met. Please incorporate a few scenarios: conservative (50% utilization), base (60%), upside (80%).

Also — procurement would like to see a clear exec escalation path in the agreement (who signs for >20% discounts, timeline for approvals, and a standard DocuSign workflow). Can you propose that in your next revision?

Best,
Rebecca Li
Head of Ops, Teladyne AI
rebecca.li@teladyne.ai

[Attachment: teladyne_usage_forecast.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Dedicated sizing impact on reserved term and GPU-cost sensitivity — Teladyne pilot

Looping in finance and product — Rebecca flagged the approval thresholds and wants both up/down protections. I ran a quick sensitivity and proposal for commercial guardrails. Key points below (draft language inlined):

Proposed guardrails (commercial intent):
- Base unit price set for 24-month term with step-down discounts tied to utilization:
  * Utilization <50%: base price (no discount)
  * Utilization 50–69%: 5% unit discount applied retro to month start
  * Utilization 70–84%: 12% unit discount applied retro to month start
  * Utilization >=85%: 18% unit discount and eligibility for priority burst capacity

- GPU market indexation (upward protection):
  * If public GPU market index rises >=20% vs. baseline in any rolling 90-day window within the first 12 months, Teladyne may elect a one-time adjustment: either reduce committed capacity by up to 25% OR enter a good-faith reprice within 30 days.
  * Any reprice request that would increase Redwood's concession (net discount) beyond 22% requires CFO sign-off (finance approval path).

- Downside sharing / rebate (if GPU market price falls >=15% over a 90-day window):
  * Option A (preferred): immediate per-unit rebate applied to forward invoices for remaining term.
  * Option B (alternative): one-time credit applied to next invoice cycle + bilateral review for contract amendment.

Approval and execution path:
- Discounts <=15%: procurement lead sign-off (Teladyne).
- Discounts >15% and <=22%: VP Procurement + Redwood Sales Director approval.
- Discounts >22%: Redwood Finance + Teladyne CFO approvals required (DocuSign path).

Risks / ask from product/ops:
- We should avoid an open-ended downward reset that forces us to refund large historical consumption. Recommend limiting rebates to forward application or capped credits equal to X months of committed spend (we modeled 3 months cap in the attached scenario).

Marissa — can you run quick P&L sensitivity showing impact of the 22% concession threshold vs. a 25% threshold (spread on unit margin and absolute $ exposure over 24 months)? Marcus — does product/ops accept the 25% reduce-capability option as operationally feasible?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

[Inline: quick math references and scenario notes]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@teladyne.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, procurement@teladyne.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 16:34:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing impact on reserved term and GPU-cost sensitivity — Teladyne pilot

Rebecca / Teladyne team,

Appreciate the clarity on approval thresholds and the forecast. I've attached a short commercial summary that reflects the internal approvals we need and the practical guardrails Redwood can accept without creating open financial liability. Highlights from our side:

- We can accept the proposed indexation and rebate mechanics with the following carve-outs:
  * Upward indexation trigger (>=20% spike) gives Teladyne the option to reduce committed capacity up to 25% OR request a reprice; Redwood will not be obligated to accept a reprice that increases Redwood's net concession beyond 22% without explicit CFO approval.
  * Downside rebate: we will issue forward credits capped at the equivalent of 3 months of committed spend (in lieu of retro refunds) unless both parties agree to a different mechanism.

- Final approval path to include explicit DocuSign routing: procurement lead -> VP Procurement (Teladyne) -> VP Sales (Redwood) -> Redwood CFO (only if discount >22%).

- Proposed commercial asks from Redwood: a minimal 60-day cure period for any market-triggered renegotiation and a single bilateral reprice window per 12-month period to avoid churn.

Please review the attached summary (Redwood_Reserved_Capacity_Term_Summary_v1.pdf). If that aligns, Sofia and I can draft the redline-ready commercial appendix for legal/procurement. If Teladyne needs exceptions to the CFO threshold, please indicate what business case (volume ramp, references, strategic partnership) would justify it.

Sofia — suggest we schedule the exec alignment call Thursday morning PT to accelerate. Rebecca / procurement — can you confirm preferred times?

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

[Attachment: Redwood_Reserved_Capacity_Term_Summary_v1.pdf]
